title: Where does the time go when a program sleeps?
question: Sleeping for 30 ms takes 30 ms, but the kernel works for a tiny part of it. What happens in between?
text: Sleeping for 30 ms takes 30 ms, but the kernel works for only a tiny part of it. What happens in between?
1. [hrtimer_nanosleep](1:hrtimer_nanosleep) sets a high-resolution timer for 30 ms from now.

2. [schedule](1:schedule): nothing to do until then, so the CPU is given away. The idle task (swapper) runs and waits for an interrupt. Look at the task strip under the timeline: the long green stretch is idle.
3. 30 ms later the timer's interrupt fires and [hrtimer_wakeup](1:hrtimer_wakeup:any) makes the sleeper runnable again; the call returns 0.
Try: [sleep for 0 ns](try:1): does it still schedule? Or [CLOCK_REALTIME](try:2) instead of CLOCK_MONOTONIC.
